label: delimiter in long (L>=8) sequences, and copy-phase inputs o/r
explanation: Sparse update-gate unit (~1% of steps) that is essentially never active in the original phase. About 45% of activation mass is on the <DEL> step, almost only when L is 8 or 9 (77% of all mass comes from L=9 sequences). The strongest activations are all at <DEL> in L=9 sequences. Most of the rest is in the copy phase when the fed-back input is o (9.5x lift) or r (5x), with a smaller rise at the last copy steps of L=9 sequences. The two-clause predicate covers about 88% of activation mass and 95% of the top quartile. Precision is low (~0.15): only ~14% of L>=8 delimiter steps and ~16% of copy-phase o/r steps are active, and which ones fire depends on sequence content that no simple token variable captured (prev_tok l/1/p/q helps a little). Does not fire for L<=6, in the original phase, or on most other copy-phase tokens.
